This directory contains examples extracted from Appendix A of RFC9711. They
have been modified slightly in order to make them conform to the text of
RFC9711, which the original examples did not.

Specifically:

- The spec describes the UEID as a type byte followed by the number of bytes
  determined by the value of the type byte. For example for randomly generated
  UEIDs, the type byte is 0x01 and is followed by either 16, 24, or 32 randomly
  generated bytes, for a total of 17 bytes. The diag examples, on the other
  hand,  specify the UEID as a 16 byte value (including the type byte). These
  values have been padded with 0x00 to make them 17 bytes. A comment is left in
  the .diag files where this was done.
- UEID values in JSON are similarly problematic and have been adjusted to be
  base64url_nopad encoding of the updated value in the diags. Since JSON does
  not permit comments, the adjustments are not marked.
- The spec defines base64-url-text as matching regular expression
  "[A-Za-z0-9_-]+", and so corresponds to base64 URL encoding WITHOUT padding.
  Original JSON examples included padding, which has been removed.
- CBOR detached EAT bundle in section A.2.2 contains invalid encoding of the
  nested token (the header is bstr(102) where as it should be bstr(103)).
- JSON detached EAT bundle in section A.2.3 was missing a comma inside encoded
  detached claims and was also using standard rather than URL base64 encoding.
- As per existing erratum https://errata.rfc-editor.org/eid8771/, "secboot" was
  renamed to "oemboot" in A.1.7.

See also: https://errata.rfc-editor.org/eid9193/
